Title: Persona
Text: Priya Nair, senior caseworker, Aurelia Social Support Agency. 160 open cases; works an inbox of registry notices, hospital summaries, employer notices, phone notes and citizen messages.

Title: Root cause
Text: The agency learns about life events but has no step that turns an event into a checked, explained offer of help. Services wait for citizens to apply, and a full check across 12 schemes takes ~45 minutes, so it only happens when someone asks.

Title: Evidence
Text: History of 320 life events: 21% enrolled within 30 days; median 65 days to a first claim; 42% claimed nothing within a year; 41% of entitled schemes ever claimed. Today: $160,770/yr unclaimed across 50 of 141 households; 40 new events, 29 with unclaimed support worth $208,720/yr. 9 records have no income; 1 duplicate; 2 messages in Spanish.

Title: Goal
Text: Find where AI genuinely helps a caseworker turn life events into timely, correct, explained offers of support, score it, and scope a safe MVP for the PRD.

Title: S1 Event arrives | Today
Text: Registry feeds, employer notices, hospital summaries, caseworker notes, citizen messages land in separate systems.

Title: S1 Event arrives | Pain
Text: Same household's facts in 7 formats; free text; Spanish and Arabic messages; nothing flags them as life events.

Title: S2 Understand the household | Today
Text: Caseworker opens the record and re-reads the source to find income, rent, partner, children.

Title: S2 Understand the household | Pain
Text: Records stale (some 2.5 years old), 9 of 141 with no income, record values conflict with the new source, 1 duplicate person.

Title: S2 Understand the household | AI opportunities
S3 Check entitlements | Today
Text: Caseworker checks thresholds in a personal spreadsheet, one scheme at a time, when a citizen asks.

Title: S3 Check entitlements | Pain
Text: ~45 minutes per full check across 12 schemes, so it isn't done for most events; easy to miss Winter Energy or School Meals.

Title: S4 Reach the citizen | Today
Text: Generic letter or 'go online and apply'; translation needs a colleague.

Title: S4 Reach the citizen | Pain
Text: Message doesn't say what they can get or why; non-English speakers drop off; risk of wrong amounts in hand-written letters.

Title: S4 Reach the citizen | AI opportunities
S5 Application | Today
Text: Citizen re-enters facts the agency already holds, finds documents, often stops halfway.

Title: S5 Application | Pain
Text: Same facts asked again per scheme; missing documents stall claims for weeks.

Title: S5 Application | AI opportunities
Text: O6

Title: S6 Decide and pay | Today
Text: Caseworker or assessor decides; discretionary schemes need judgement.

Title: S6 Decide and pay | Pain
Text: Disability and hardship cases need a person; crises (eviction, power cut) buried in the inbox.

Title: S6 Decide and pay | AI opportunities
S7 Track and learn | Today
Text: Monthly reporting on claims, not on take-up after events.

Title: S7 Track and learn | Pain
Text: No one measures how many eligible households got support, or how fast.

Title: S7 Track and learn | AI opportunities
Text: O8

Title: O1 Read facts from any source
Text: Pull household facts (job end date, income, rent, partner status, care hours, crisis) from free-text sources in any language, each with a verbatim quote. Why AI: Structured extraction from messy multilingual text is a core LLM strength and every fact can be checked against its quote. Evidence: 40 events in 7 formats; 2 Spanish messages Stage: S1-S2

Title: O2 Life-event triage queue
Text: Rank today's events: crisis first, then unreadable messages, then value of unclaimed support. Why AI: Ranking is transparent rules over O1 + O4 output; AI only supplies the crisis flag. Evidence: 1 eviction + power cut buried among 40 events Stage: S1

Title: O3 Record update with conflicts shown
Text: Apply new facts to a copy of the record, newest source wins, and show what changed (record $47,000 vs source $33,000). Why AI: Uses O1 facts; the logic is code. Evidence: stale records, 9 with no income Stage: S2

Title: O4 Full entitlement check, every scheme
Text: Check all 12 schemes on every event and cite the clause for each pass, fail or missing fact. Why AI: Deliberately NOT AI: eligibility is law, so it is deterministic code. AI feeds it facts. Evidence: 45-minute manual check; 41% take-up of entitlements Stage: S3

Title: O5 Plain-language outreach in the citizen's language
Text: Draft a warm, short message listing what they may get and what to send, in their language, using only amounts from the rules. Why AI: LLM drafting and translation are mature; the risk is invented amounts, so a safety check withholds any unsupported figure. Evidence: 7 languages on the caseload; 68 of 141 prefer a language other than English; generic letters Stage: S4

Title: O6 Pre-filled applications
Text: Fill each scheme's application from the record and the event, listing only the documents still needed. Why AI: Mostly data mapping; low AI risk, high time saving. Evidence: citizens re-enter known facts per scheme Stage: S5

Title: O7 Route to a caseworker
Text: Send discretionary schemes (Disability Support, Hardship Grant) to a person with the reason, never as 'eligible'. Why AI: AI detects the crisis or medical signal; the decision stays human. Evidence: eviction, power cut, stroke discharges Stage: S6

Title: O8 Take-up gap and North Star dashboard
Text: Show unclaimed support by scheme and enrolment within 30 days of an event. Why AI: Reporting over rule outputs; little AI. Evidence: nobody measures take-up after events Stage: S7

Title: O9 Detect events from bank or tax data
Text: Infer job loss or hardship from income drops in tax or bank feeds. Why AI: Powerful but needs data-sharing law and consent the agency doesn't have; surveillance risk. Evidence: none in dataset Stage: S1

Title: O10 Auto-merge duplicate records
Text: Merge records that look like the same person. Why AI: Fuzzy matching works, but a wrong merge mixes two people's benefits. Flag, don't merge. Evidence: 1 duplicate (same name and birth date) Stage: S2

Title: O11 Auto-award eligible benefits
Text: Pay benefits automatically when the rules say eligible. Why AI: Technically simple, but legally a decision needs a person today, and stale records make silent awards risky. Evidence: the new source contradicts the record in 17 of 40 events Stage: S3

Title: O12 Auto-send outreach
Text: Send messages to citizens without review. Why AI: One wrong amount or a message to someone who opted out damages trust in the agency. Evidence: 1 person opted out of contact Stage: S4

Title: O13 Citizen chatbot for eligibility
Text: A public chatbot that answers 'what can I get?'. Why AI: Useful later, but it is still 'pull'; the root cause is the agency not acting on what it knows. Evidence: root cause is no proactive step Stage: S4

Title: O14 Fraud risk scoring
Text: Score citizens for fraud risk while checking eligibility. Why AI: Mixes help with suspicion, high bias risk, and not the problem we found. Evidence: none Stage: S6

Title: Scoring rubric
Text: Impact (1-5): households and money affected + how often it happens + strength of dataset evidence. Feasibility (1-5): data available in the dataset + maturity of the AI technique + cost of being wrong + prototype effort. Score = Impact x Feasibility (max 25). Do first = Impact >= 4 and Feasibility >= 4.

Title: Should do
Text: Read every life-event source the agency already receives, in any language, and nothing else.

Title: Should do
Text: Pull out facts with the exact quote they came from; drop any fact without one.

Title: Should do
Text: Check all 12 schemes on every event and cite the clause behind each result.

Title: Should do
Text: Ask the citizen for a missing fact (income, savings, childcare fees) instead of guessing.

Title: Should do
Text: Draft plain-language outreach in the citizen's language and pre-fill applications for approval.

Title: Should do
Text: Put crises and unreadable messages at the top of the queue for a person.

Title: Should do
Text: Show where the record and the new source disagree.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Decide eligibility: the rules engine does, from law, in code.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Award, pay or refuse any benefit.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Send any message to a citizen without a caseworker's approval.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Contact anyone who opted out of proactive contact.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Mark Disability Support or Hardship Grant as eligible; they always go to a person.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Use gender, ethnicity, religion or nationality, or score people for fraud.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Pull data from bank, tax or social media sources it has no legal basis to use.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Merge or change the master record on its own.

Title: F1 Read the event
Text: From: O1, O2 | AI capability: Structured extraction to a fixed schema (14 fields) with verbatim quotes; multilingual | Inputs: Event source text + registry fields | Output: Facts with quote and confidence; crisis flag; 'unclear' list | Guardrails: No quote, no fact (quote must be found in the source); registry fields trusted as given; free-text source with no facts goes to 'Read now'. | Human in loop: Caseworker sees each quote highlighted in the source | Test: Fact recall >= 90% on 79 labelled facts; 0 facts without a verified quote

Title: F2 Check every scheme
Text: From: O3, O4, O7 | AI capability: None (deterministic rules engine), fed by F1 | Inputs: Record + F1 facts | Output: Per scheme: Eligible / Needs info / Caseworker decides, with clause citations, amount and missing facts | Guardrails: Eligibility only from code; missing fact = question, never a guess; discretionary schemes never 'eligible'; conflicts with the record shown. | Human in loop: Caseworker ticks which applications to open | Test: Precision >= 95% and recall >= 90% vs independent labels on 40 events; 0 caseworker-only schemes marked eligible

Title: F3 Draft the outreach
Text: From: O5 | AI capability: Grounded generation and translation from a JSON of rule results | Inputs: Eligible and needs-info schemes, amounts, documents, questions, language | Output: Short message in the citizen's language | Guardrails: Safety check withholds drafts with any amount not from the rules, other schemes, promises, or caseworker-only schemes; no draft for opted-out people; checks re-run on every edit. | Human in loop: Caseworker edits and approves; nothing is sent automatically | Test: 100% of offline drafts pass; 4 of 4 red-team drafts blocked

Title: F4 Pre-fill and log
Text: From: O6, O8 | AI capability: Data mapping (no model) | Inputs: Record, facts, chosen schemes | Output: Pre-filled applications; audit entry; take-up dashboard | Guardrails: Only documents still needed are requested; every approval and rejection logged with who and when. | Human in loop: Citizen confirms the application | Test: Every approval produces a log entry

Title: Next (post-MVP)
Text: From: O10, O13 | AI capability: Duplicate detection; citizen-facing assistant on the same rules | Inputs: Records; citizen questions | Output: Merge suggestions; answers with clause citations | Guardrails: Same as F2/F3 | Human in loop: Records officer approves merges | Test: After MVP proves extraction quality

Title: Global guardrail
Text: The AI reads and writes; the rules decide; a person approves.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Grounded only: every fact quotes its source; every amount comes from the rules.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Uncertainty is visible: missing facts become questions; unreadable messages go to a person.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Least data: only sources the agency already receives; no protected characteristics in context; no training on citizen data.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Consent: no proactive contact for people who opted out.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Audit trail: every suggestion, approval and rejection logged with who and when.

Title: Risk: A wrong amount reaches a citizen
Text: Mitigation: Safety check on every draft and every edit; withheld drafts can't be approved

Title: Risk: A crisis is missed
Text: Mitigation: Crisis flag ranks it first; unreadable messages ranked 'Read now'; eval: 0 silent misses

Title: Risk: Stale record gives a wrong result
Text: Mitigation: Newer source wins and the conflict is shown; caseworker confirms with the citizen

Title: Risk: Bias against some groups
Text: Mitigation: Protected characteristics excluded; rules are law in code; monitor take-up by region and language

Title: Risk: Caseworkers rubber-stamp
Text: Mitigation: Clauses and quotes on screen; track edit and rejection rates; spot-check 5% of approvals

Title: Risk: Citizens feel watched
Text: Mitigation: Only events the agency already receives; clear opt-out; message explains why we're writing

Title: Step 3 PRD
Text: North Star = eligible households enrolled within 30 days of a life event (21% today, 60% target at full rollout). Supporting: minutes per review (45 to 10), suggestion approval rate (85%+), entitlement precision (95%+) and recall (90%+), fact recall (90%+), 0 unsupported amounts sent, 0 messages to opted-out people.
